series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 01/12] mm/page_alloc: reset can_retry_reserves when the slowpath restarts
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series aims to improve the page allocation mechanism in the Linux kernel by resetting the can_retry_reserves flag when the slowpath restarts after a cpuset update or zonelist rebuild. This change ensures that the retry still runs at most once per change, preventing potential issues with reclaiming memory.

review_comments.author: Zi Yan
review_comments.summary: Identified the patch as correct and suitable for merge, with no further comments or concerns.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Sat Oct 31, 2026 at 10:13 PM EDT, Gregory Price (Meta) wrote:
> Commit 2c4c3e29897d ("mm/page_alloc: simplify __alloc_pages_slowpath()
> flow") retries an allocation once with reserve_flags when the caller
> becomes eligible for reserves, guarded by can_retry_reserves.
>
> A restart after a cpuset update or a zonelist rebuild retries with
> can_retry_reserves already set to false, so a caller that cannot
> reclaim (GFP_NOWAIT | __GFP_MEMALLOC), fails without trying reserves.
>
> Reset can_retry_reserves on restart. Only a cpuset or zonelist change
> restarts the slowpath, so the retry still runs at most once per change.
>
> With a kprobe helping to make the race deterministic, an allocation
> can be made to return NULL. With this patch the allocation will succeed.
>
> Fixes: 2c4c3e29897d ("mm/page_alloc: simplify __alloc_pages_slowpath() flow")
> Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
> Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
> ---
>  mm/page_alloc.c | 3 ++-
>  1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
>

LGTM.

Acked-by: Zi Yan <ziy@nvidia.com>

-- 
Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 02/12] mm/page_alloc: keep the pagesets of an empty zone
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series aims to improve the handling of zone pagesets in the Linux kernel. Specifically, it addresses an issue where the per-cpu pageset is freed when a zone becomes empty, leading to potential corruption or leaks. The patches modify various functions to keep the pagesets intact and reuse them when the zone gets memory again.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 03/12] mm, page_alloc: pass zone pointer to trace_reclaim_retry_zone
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series addresses memory hotplug rebuilds of zonelists while allocations are under way, which can lead to incorrect zone indexing in the tracepoint reclaim_retry_zone. The patch passes the zone pointer instead of the zoneref pointer to fix this issue.

review_comments.author: Zi Yan
review_comments.summary: Identified a potential issue in memory hotplug rebuilds of zonelists and agreed that passing the zone pointer is a good solution to fix it.
review_comments.raw_body:

> From: Josef Bacik <josef@toxicpanda.com>
>
> should_reclaim_retry() walks a zonelist and passes the zoneref pointer
> to the reclaim_retry_zone tracepoint, which loads the zone from the
> entry again to find the node.
>
> Memory hotplug rebuilds the zonelists in place while allocations are
> under way. When a zone in front of the zoneref entry has become empty,

> tracepoint looks at it. zonelist_node_idx() then dereferences a NULL

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 04/12] mm/page_alloc: detect zonelist rebuilds from memory hot-add
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses a race condition between build_all_zonelists and page allocation by gating sequence checks on CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTPLUG, which covers all configurations that rebuild zonelists after boot.

review_comments.author: Zi Yan
review_comments.summary: Acknowledged the patch without any objections or concerns.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Sat Oct 31, 2026 at 10:13 PM EDT, Gregory Price (Meta) wrote:
> The zonelist_update_seq retry was limited to CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTREMOVE,
> presumably because only hot-remove takes zones out of a zonelist.
>
> However, build_zonerefs_node() rewrites the zonelists in place, so
> onlining the first block of a zone shifts the entries that follow it
> in every zonelist containing that zone.  This can cause a spurious
> allocation failure for a __GFP_THISNODE caller.
>
> For a node with only ZONE_NORMAL, onlining its first ZONE_MOVABLE block
> rewrites the node's ZONELIST_NOFALLBACK list as:
>
>   [NORMAL, NULL] -> [MOVABLE, NULL] -> [MOVABLE, NORMAL, NULL]
>
> A concurrent GFP_KERNEL | __GFP_THISNODE allocation can observe the
> intermediate list, skip ZONE_MOVABLE, and find no eligible zone. With
> CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTREMOVE=n, check_retry_zonelist() returns 0 and the
> allocation fails even though the node has free ZONE_NORMAL memory.
>
> Gate the sequence checks on CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTPLUG, which covers every
> configuration that rebuilds zonelists after boot.
>
> Fixes: 3d36424b3b58 ("mm/page_alloc: fix race condition between build_all_zonelists and page allocation")
> Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
> Reviewed-by: Vlastimil Babka (SUSE) <vbabka@kernel.org>

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 05/12] mm/mmzone: read the zoneref slot once in zonelist_zone()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch updates the zonelist_zone() function to use READ_ONCE() when loading a zone from a zoneref slot, ensuring that the loaded zone is not changed by memory hotplug rebuilds of the zonelists. This prevents issues where a caller checks one zone and then uses another or the NULL terminator due to multiple loads of the same slot. The patch addresses a problem introduced in a previous commit (11cd8638c37f) that removed stop_machine from build_all_zonelists.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 06/12] mm/page_alloc: snapshot the preferred zone against shrink rebuilds
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a kernel NULL pointer dereference bug by snapshotting the preferred zone against shrink rebuilds in the get_page_from_freelist() function. The preferred zone is read only once, as concurrent zonelist rebuilds can null or replace it. This ensures that even if the preferred zone's slot is rebuilt, the function will still work correctly.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 07/12] mm/mmzone: read each zoneref slot once when filtering by nodemask
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug where the kernel would dereference a NULL pointer when filtering by nodemask, caused by reading each zoneref slot twice in the __next_zones_zonelist function. The fix is to read each slot only once and test its zone directly. This change also removes unnecessary code paths for non-NUMA configurations.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 08/12] mm/page_alloc: retry allocations that raced with a zonelist rebuild
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses a problem where GFP_KERNEL allocations can land in the wrong zone due to concurrent zonelist rebuilds. It introduces a new function, `check_retry_zonelist`, which checks if the zonelist has changed since the allocation was made and retries the allocation if necessary. This is done by freeing the allocated page and retrying the allocation. The patch also adds a new function, `zonelist_iter_sample`, which samples the zonelist sequence number without waiting for the writer to finish. This allows for faster allocation paths to detect concurrent rebuilds and retry allocations accordingly.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 09/12] mm/hugetlb: retry the pool walk when the zonelist is rebuilt
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses a problem where a hugetlb fault bound to one node can take a pool page from another due to the way the zonelist is rebuilt during zone onlining. The patch introduces checks for zonelist updates and retries the pool walk if the zonelist has changed, ensuring that pages are taken from the correct node. This change fixes an issue where kprobes holding the walk across the online could cause a fault to take a page from the wrong node.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 10/12] mm/page_alloc: retry alloc_contig_pages() when the zonelist is rebuilt
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the alloc_contig_frozen_pages_noprof function to retry when the zonelist is rebuilt during a zone rebuild operation. This change ensures that gigantic hugetlb pages are not allocated in ZONE_MOVABLE, and instead are placed in ZONE_NORMAL. The patch also adds checks for zonelist updates before using each zone, and restarts the walk if it has changed. This approach addresses issues with kprobes holding the walk across online operations, and improves the allocation of gigantic pages.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 11/12] mm/mempolicy: read the zoneref slot once in mempolicy_slab_node()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the mempolicy_slab_node() function by reading the zoneref slot only once, instead of twice. This prevents a kernel NULL pointer dereference bug that occurs when a movable block in the zonelist goes offline while a task's slab_strict_numa allocation is held between two reads. The fix involves storing the zone reference in a variable and reusing it to look up the node's index.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 12/12] mm/mmzone: remove zonelist_node_idx()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch removes the zonelist_node_idx() helper function from the Linux kernel, which was used to return the index of a node for an entry in the zonelist. The function is deemed unnecessary because it loads the zone from the slot again, which can lead to inconsistencies when memory hotplug rewrites zonelists in place. The patch open-codes the functionality in its two remaining callers, neither of which can race with a rebuild. Additionally, one of the callers has unreachable code due to the conditions under which it is called.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series addresses memory hotplug-related races and issues in the Linux kernel's memory allocator. The patches fix problems such as zone list rebuilds, page set freeing, and allocation failures that can occur when memory is added or removed from a system while allocations are happening. The approach taken involves fixing specific walkers and functions to ensure correct behavior during these operations, including removing a helper function that invites the same bug. The patches were tested on a QEMU guest with three NUMA nodes and showed improved results compared to an unmodified kernel.

review_comments.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
review_comments.summary: The author is addressing a concern about the retry mechanism in __alloc_pages_slowpath() not working correctly when can_retry_reserves is already set to false after a restart. The author agrees that this is an issue and proposes resetting can_retry_reserves on restart, ensuring that the retry runs at most once per change.

review_comments.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the reclaim_retry_zone tracepoint dereferencing a NULL zone pointer when memory hotplug rebuilds zonelists in place. They agreed to pass the zone pointer instead of the zoneref pointer, which fixes the issue.
review_comments.raw_body:
From: Josef Bacik <josef@toxicpanda.com>

should_reclaim_retry() walks a zonelist and passes the zoneref pointer
to the reclaim_retry_zone tracepoint, which loads the zone from the
entry again to find the node.

Memory hotplug rebuilds the zonelists in place while allocations are
under way. When a zone in front of the zoneref entry has become empty,
the entries move up, and this one can be the end marker by the time the
tracepoint looks at it. zonelist_node_idx() then dereferences a NULL
zone. Short of that, the event can name another zone than the one its
numbers belong to.

Pass the zone pointer instead of the zoneref pointer.

Fixes: d379f01de095 ("oom, trace: add oom detection tracepoints")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Assisted-by: LLM
Signed-off-by: Josef Bacik <josef@toxicpanda.com>
Signed-off-by: David Hildenbrand (Arm) <david@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Vlastimil Babka (SUSE) <vbabka@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 include/trace/events/oom.h | 8 ++++----
 mm/page_alloc.c            | 2 +-
 2 files changed, 5 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)

diff --git a/include/trace/events/oom.h b/include/trace/events/oom.h
index 9f0a5d1482c4..cbcf6fe4cc61 100644
--- a/include/trace/events/oom.h
+++ b/include/trace/events/oom.h
@@ -33,7 +33,7 @@ TRACE_EVENT(oom_score_adj_update,
 
 TRACE_EVENT(reclaim_retry_zone,
 
-	TP_PROTO(struct zoneref *zoneref,
+	TP_PROTO(struct zone *zone,
 		int order,
 		unsigned long reclaimable,
 		unsigned long available,
@@ -41,7 +41,7 @@ TRACE_EVENT(reclaim_retry_zone,
 		int no_progress_loops,
 		bool wmark_check),
 
-	TP_ARGS(zoneref, order, reclaimable, available, min_wmark, no_progress_loops, wmark_check),
+	TP_ARGS(zone, order, reclaimable, available, min_wmark, no_progress_loops, wmark_check),
 
 	TP_STRUCT__entry(
 		__field(	int, node)
@@ -55,8 +55,8 @@ TRACE_EVENT(reclaim_retry_zone,
 	),
 
 	TP_fast_assign(
-		__entry->node = zonelist_node_idx(zoneref);
-		__entry->zone_idx = zonelist_zone_idx(zoneref);
+		__entry->node = zone_to_nid(zone);
+		__entry->zone_idx = zone_idx(zone);
 		__entry->order = order;
 		__entry->reclaimable = reclaimable;
 		__entry->available = available;
diff --git a/mm/page_alloc.c b/mm/page_alloc.c
index 1850a41f24f7..e14d550d4128 100644
--- a/mm/page_alloc.c
+++ b/mm/page_alloc.c
@@ -4670,7 +4670,7 @@ should_reclaim_retry(gfp_t gfp_mask, unsigned order,
 		 */
 		wmark = __zone_watermark_ok(zone, order, min_wmark,
 				ac->highest_zoneidx, alloc_flags, available);
-		trace_reclaim_retry_zone(z, order, reclaimable,
+		trace_reclaim_retry_zone(zone, order, reclaimable,
 				available, min_wmark, *no_progress_loops, wmark);
 		if (wmark) {
 			ret = true;
-- 
2.56.0

review_comments.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern that the zonelist_update_seq retry was limited to CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTREMOVE, but this led to spurious allocation failures for __GFP_THISNODE callers when onlining zones. The author agreed to gate the sequence checks on CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTPLUG instead.
review_comments.raw_body:
The zonelist_update_seq retry was limited to CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTREMOVE,
presumably because only hot-remove takes zones out of a zonelist.

However, build_zonerefs_node() rewrites the zonelists in place, so
onlining the first block of a zone shifts the entries that follow it
in every zonelist containing that zone.  This can cause a spurious
allocation failure for a __GFP_THISNODE caller.

For a node with only ZONE_NORMAL, onlining its first ZONE_MOVABLE block
rewrites the node's ZONELIST_NOFALLBACK list as:

  [NORMAL, NULL] -> [MOVABLE, NULL] -> [MOVABLE, NORMAL, NULL]

A concurrent GFP_KERNEL | __GFP_THISNODE allocation can observe the
intermediate list, skip ZONE_MOVABLE, and find no eligible zone. With
CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTREMOVE=n, check_retry_zonelist() returns 0 and the
allocation fails even though the node has free ZONE_NORMAL memory.

Gate the sequence checks on CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTPLUG, which covers every
configuration that rebuilds zonelists after boot.

Fixes: 3d36424b3b58 ("mm/page_alloc: fix race condition between build_all_zonelists and page allocation")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reviewed-by: Vlastimil Babka (SUSE) <vbabka@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 mm/page_alloc.c | 4 ++--
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/mm/page_alloc.c b/mm/page_alloc.c
index e14d550d4128..11be12b443ad 100644
--- a/mm/page_alloc.c
+++ b/mm/page_alloc.c
@@ -4404,7 +4404,7 @@ static DEFINE_SEQLOCK(zonelist_update_seq);
 
 static unsigned int zonelist_iter_begin(void)
 {
-	if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTREMOVE))
+	if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTPLUG))
 		return read_seqbegin(&zonelist_update_seq);
 
 	return 0;
@@ -4412,7 +4412,7 @@ static unsigned int zonelist_iter_begin(void)
 
 static unsigned int check_retry_zonelist(unsigned int seq)
 {
-	if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTREMOVE))
+	if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTPLUG))
 		return read_seqretry(&zonelist_update_seq, seq);
 
 	return seq;
-- 
2.56.0

review_comments.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
review_comments.summary: The author is addressing a concern about the swapoff path dropping the per-vswap spinlock before calling try_to_unmap(). They acknowledged that this is necessary to prevent corruption of per-cpu memory, and explained that the pagesets are only freed because setup_zone_pageset() would otherwise leak them. The author plans to keep the pagesets instead and let setup_zone_pageset() use them again when the zone gets memory.
review_comments.raw_body:
From: Josef Bacik <josef@toxicpanda.com>

When the last memory of a zone goes offline, zone_pcp_reset() frees
zone->per_cpu_pageset and zone->per_cpu_zonestats. Nothing waits for those
who found the zone populated and still use the two pointers. They take
neither the memory hotplug lock nor any other lock which offline_pages()
holds, and some of them can sleep:

  CPU0 vmstat_update()                CPU1 offline_pages()
  refresh_cpu_vm_stats()
    for_each_populated_zone(zone)
      pcp = zone->per_cpu_pageset
      cond_resched()
                                      adjust_present_page_count()
                                      zone_pcp_reset(zone)
                                        free_percpu(zone->per_cpu_pageset)
      decay_pcp_high(zone, pcp)
      __this_cpu_write(pcp->expire, 0)

The same goes for drain_all_pages(NULL), which takes pcp->lock, for
zone_pcp_update(), show_free_areas() and the readers and writers of the
zonestats. If the per-cpu memory has got a new owner in the meantime, it
is corrupted.

The pagesets are only freed because setup_zone_pageset() would otherwise
leak them when the zone gets memory again. Keep them instead and let
setup_zone_pageset() and zone_pcp_init() use them again, like it is done
with pgdat->per_cpu_nodestats. Their lists are empty, and their limits
have been calculated for a zone without memory by the
init_per_zone_wmark_min() of offline_pages(), which is what
setup_zone_pageset() would come up with as well.

Fixes: 340175b7d14d ("mm/hotplug: free zone->pageset when a zone becomes empty")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Assisted-by: LLM
Signed-off-by: Josef Bacik <josef@toxicpanda.com>
Signed-off-by: David Hildenbrand (Arm) <david@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Johannes Weiner <hannes@cmpxchg.org>
Signed-off-by: Vlastimil Babka (SUSE) <vbabka@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 mm/page_alloc.c | 20 ++++++++++++++------
 1 file changed, 14 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)

diff --git a/mm/page_alloc.c b/mm/page_alloc.c
index f1048168c90c..1850a41f24f7 100644
--- a/mm/page_alloc.c
+++ b/mm/page_alloc.c
@@ -6308,6 +6308,10 @@ void __meminit setup_zone_pageset(struct zone *zone)
 {
 	int cpu;
 
+	/* The zone has been populated before, see zone_pcp_reset(). */
+	if (zone->per_cpu_pageset != &boot_pageset)
+		return;
+
 	/* Size may be 0 on !SMP && !NUMA */
 	if (sizeof(struct per_cpu_zonestat) > 0)
 		zone->per_cpu_zonestats = alloc_percpu(struct per_cpu_zonestat);
@@ -6400,6 +6404,10 @@ void __init setup_per_cpu_pageset(void)
 
 __meminit void zone_pcp_init(struct zone *zone)
 {
+	/* A node which is added again, see zone_pcp_reset(). */
+	if (zone->per_cpu_pageset && zone->per_cpu_pageset != &boot_pageset)
+		return;
+
 	/*
 	 * per cpu subsystem is not up at this point. The following code
 	 * relies on the ability of the linker to provide the
@@ -7680,6 +7688,12 @@ void zone_pcp_enable(struct zone *zone)
 	mutex_unlock(&pcp_batch_high_lock);
 }
 
+/*
+ * The zone has become empty. Its pagesets and zonestats are not freed: nothing
+ * keeps somebody who found the zone populated, such as refresh_cpu_vm_stats()
+ * or drain_all_pages(), from still using them. They are used again when the
+ * zone gets memory again.
+ */
 void zone_pcp_reset(struct zone *zone)
 {
 	int cpu;
@@ -7690,12 +7704,6 @@ void zone_pcp_reset(struct zone *zone)
 			pzstats = per_cpu_ptr(zone->per_cpu_zonestats, cpu);
 			drain_zonestat(zone, pzstats);
 		}
-		free_percpu(zone->per_cpu_pageset);
-		zone->per_cpu_pageset = &boot_pageset;
-		if (zone->per_cpu_zonestats != &boot_zonestats) {
-			free_percpu(zone->per_cpu_zonestats);
-			zone->per_cpu_zonestats = &boot_zonestats;
-		}
 	}
 }

review_comments.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the compiler reordering loads of a zoneref slot, which could lead to using an incorrect zone or NULL pointer. They proposed using READ_ONCE() to ensure a single load and prevent this issue.
review_comments.raw_body:
Memory hotplug rebuilds zonelists in place while allocations walk them,
so a zoneref slot can change between two loads of it.

zonelist_zone() loads the slot with a plain access.  The compiler may
load it again later instead of keeping the zone it already read, so a
caller can check one zone and then use another, or the NULL terminator.

Use READ_ONCE().  Callers that take a zone from a slot and keep using
it, such as get_page_from_freelist() with ac->preferred_zoneref, need
that single load.

Fixes: 11cd8638c37f ("mm, page_alloc: remove stop_machine from build_all_zonelists")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 include/linux/mmzone.h | 3 ++-
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/include/linux/mmzone.h b/include/linux/mmzone.h
index ecd1ebd49756..4bc2318ac37f 100644
--- a/include/linux/mmzone.h
+++ b/include/linux/mmzone.h
@@ -1855,7 +1855,8 @@ extern struct zone *next_zone(struct zone *zone);
 
 static inline struct zone *zonelist_zone(struct zoneref *zoneref)
 {
-	return zoneref->zone;
+	/* Memory hotplug rewrites zonelists in place. */
+	return READ_ONCE(zoneref->zone);
 }
 
 static inline int zonelist_zone_idx(const struct zoneref *zoneref)
-- 
2.56.0

review_comments.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the __next_zones_zonelist() function reading a slot twice, which can lead to a NULL pointer dereference when offlining a zone's last block. The author explained that current GCC and clang merge the two reads, but nothing requires it, and provided an example where holding a nodemask allocation between the reads causes an oops. They agreed to restructure the code in v2 to read the slot only once.
review_comments.raw_body:
__next_zones_zonelist() tests a slot's zone for NULL, then reads the
slot again to look up the zone's node. Offlining a zone's last block
rebuilds the zonelists in place, so the second read can return the
terminator:

  CPU 0                             CPU 1
  __next_zones_zonelist(nodemask)
    zonelist_zone(slot 1) = NORMAL
                                    offline_pages()
                                      build_all_zonelists()
                                        [MOVABLE, NORMAL, NULL]
                                        -> [NORMAL, NULL]
    zref_in_nodemask(slot 1)
      zone_to_nid(NULL)

Current GCC and clang merge the two reads, but nothing requires it.
With mm/mmzone.o built with -fno-inline -fno-ipa-sra, holding a
nodemask allocation between the reads while the node's last movable
block goes offline oopses every time:

  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000060
  RIP: 0010:zone_to_nid+0x0/0x10
  Call Trace:
   zref_in_nodemask+0x9/0x20
   __next_zones_zonelist+0x23/0x70
   prepare_alloc_pages.constprop.0+0x16c/0x190
   __alloc_frozen_pages_noprof+0xaf/0x330

Read the slot once and test that zone. A NULL zone still ends the walk.

Fixes: 11cd8638c37f ("mm, page_alloc: remove stop_machine from build_all_zonelists")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
Reviewed-by: Vlastimil Babka (SUSE) <vbabka@kernel.org>
---
 mm/mmzone.c | 11 ++++++-----
 1 file changed, 6 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)

diff --git a/mm/mmzone.c b/mm/mmzone.c
index 9cc9ef588580..65880396f104 100644
--- a/mm/mmzone.c
+++ b/mm/mmzone.c
@@ -43,13 +43,14 @@ struct zone *next_zone(struct zone *zone)
 	return zone;
 }
 
-static inline int zref_in_nodemask(struct zoneref *zref,
-				   const nodemask_t *nodes)
+/* A NULL zone terminates the zonelist, so it ends the search. */
+static inline bool zone_in_nodemask(const struct zone *zone,
+				    const nodemask_t *nodes)
 {
 #ifdef CONFIG_NUMA
-	return node_isset(zonelist_node_idx(zref), *nodes);
+	return !zone || node_isset(zone_to_nid(zone), *nodes);
 #else
-	return 1;
+	return true;
 #endif /* CONFIG_NUMA */
 }
 
@@ -67,7 +68,7 @@ struct zoneref *__next_zones_zonelist(struct zoneref *z,
 			z++;
 	else
 		while (zonelist_zone_idx(z) > highest_zoneidx ||
-				(zonelist_zone(z) && !zref_in_nodemask(z, nodes)))
+		       !zone_in_nodemask(zonelist_zone(z), nodes))
 			z++;
 
 	return z;
--

review_comments.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the allocator loading an ineligible zone during memory hotplug, explained that this can happen when a rebuild occurs during an allocation walk and proposed adding checks to free pages if the zonelist has changed since the last check. The author agreed to add these checks in future revisions.

review_comments.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about dequeue_hugetlb_folio_nodemask() taking a pool page from the wrong node by introducing a seqlock to protect zonelist updates and checking for retry before using each zone, agreeing that this change fixes the issue.

review_comments.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about concurrent zonelist rebuilds causing NULL or replaced preferred zone slots in get_page_from_freelist() and alloc_pages_bulk_noprof(). They explained that reading the slot once keeps a usable zone, as zones are never freed. The changes read the preferred zone only once and handle stale or NULL slots by failing the same way as walking off the end.
